solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Swimming-pool, cycling, some dancing's included …

indicators.note: the cycled pool is taken inside the dance word, which holds it

parts.note: the hay (or hey) is an old country dance, so some dancing gives HAY

indicators.note: the pool's letters go round like a wheel, the front pair carried to the back

parts.note: a lido is an open-air public swimming pool

explanation.surface: A list of the pleasures of a summer break: a pool, bike rides and a bit of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' sends the first two letters of the pool to its back, making OLID, and 'included' sets that inside the dance. The hay is an old English country dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming, bike rides and dancing are the stuff of a vacation, so the whole clue paints a time off work.

clue.text: From clique's masquerade balls I abstracted an expression of genius

indicators.note: balls is read as the verb meaning messes up, so the letters get thrown into disorder
abstracted means taken away, so the I is removed from the pool before the rearranging

parts.note: these letters, with the apostrophe ignored, form the pool of letters to rework
the letter I is the one taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: Someone at a fancy-dress ball run by a clique pulls out a stroke of brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from CLIQUESMASQUERADE ('I abstracted'), then rearrange the remaining sixteen letters ('balls') into the equation written out in words.
explanation.definitionFit: Einstein's mass-energy equation is the most famous formula of the archetypal genius.

clue.text: See 2
Nothing so wordy, I forged place among records

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters before it are remade

explanation.surface: A writer boasts that, by cutting the verbiage, they made their mark in the annals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forged' rearranges the fifteen letters of NOTHING SO WORDY I.
explanation.definitionFit: To be remembered for ever is to earn a lasting spot in the chronicles of the past.

clue.text: Woman for whom, as before, temperature rises

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the pieces are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A woman whose fever is climbing again, just as it did last time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns the whole run upwards, which in a down entry means reading it from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, borne for example by the saint of Ávila.

clue.text: See 16
See 16
Land private hospital £20 after repositioning taps?

indicators.note: repositioning means putting each in the other's place, so the hot and cold letters trade spots
taps in a basin are marked H and C for hot and cold, so these two letters are the ones in play

parts.note: a nursing or rest home is a private hospital, so HOME
twenty is a score, so twenty pounds gives A SCORE

explanation.surface: Someone complains of paying twenty pounds at a private clinic just to have the taps moved.
explanation.walkthrough: HOME + A SCORE gives HOMEASCORE; 'repositioning taps' swaps the H and C, the letters on hot and cold taps, so it reads with C first and H later.
explanation.definitionFit: To come ashore is to step off a boat onto dry ground, which is the verb land.

clue.text: I felt that you changed, but only a little

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside the phrase you changed

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a friend has altered, though not by much.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across yOU CHanged. 'I felt that' is what you say when something hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of pain is the speaker's way of reporting that a blow registered.

clue.text: Kenya's capital is, I think, fashionable city on Lake Victoria

indicators.note: the capital, or head letter, of the word Kenya is wanted

parts.note: taken as written
um is the hesitant noise of someone thinking
U means upper-class or fashionable

explanation.surface: A traveller hesitantly guesses the seat of government of an East African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kenya's capital' wants to be NAIROBI, but it is just the letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kisumu is a port and Kenya's third city, on the shore of the great East African lake.

clue.text: More than enthusiastic spanking here, man's climax delayed

indicators.note: delayed means the letter arrives later, moving further back in the word

parts.note: a child is spanked over the knee, so the place of spanking is OVER KNEE

indicators.note: the climax of a word is its final letter, here the end of man

explanation.surface: A risqué scene of corporal punishment with a man's pleasure held back.
explanation.walkthrough: OVER KNEE with its N ('man's climax', the last letter of man) 'delayed', moved one place later, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being excessively eager is going beyond keenness, the sense of too enthusiastic.

clue.text: Wanting something hot, coven worked final touch to spell around

definitions.text: Wanting something hot, coven worked final touch to spell around

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word coven loses the hot thing

parts.note: an oven is a hot appliance

indicators.note: worked means kneaded or manipulated, so these letters are reshaped
the final touch to a word is its last letter, here the end of spell

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Witches stir up a final ingredient for their spell while longing for something to heat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' strips the hot appliance from the witches' group, leaving C; 'worked' rearranges L, the end of spell, with the word around, giving AULDRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches famously brew their spells in a great heated pot over a fire.

clue.text: Acts in an absurd way

indicators.note: arranged in a ridiculous fashion, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone behaves ridiculously.
explanation.walkthrough: The six letters of ACTS IN are rearranged, signalled by 'an absurd way', and the whole clue also defines the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly capers and pranks are exactly ridiculous behaviour.

clue.text: See 16
Restricted by diet, one barely feeds a little shop-girl

indicators.note: feeds means goes into, so the dieting piece is put inside the little one

parts.note: a mite is a little one, a small creature or child

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in by, so the middle of one goes inside diet

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: barely means stripped of its edges, so only the centre of the word one is kept

explanation.surface: A dieter, almost naked, feeds a small girl who works in a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' strips one to N; 'Restricted by' hems it inside the diet to make DINET, and 'feeds' pushes that into the little one.
explanation.definitionFit: A midinette is a Parisian seamstress or shop assistant, a young working woman of the fashion trade.

clue.text: This is basic, unless you count the biology of Eruca vesicaria

definitions.text: This is basic, unless you count the biology of Eruca vesicaria

parts.words: This is basic, unless you count the biology of Eruca vesicaria
parts.note: the stock phrase for something simple is read literally: Eruca vesicaria is the salad plant called ...

explanation.surface: Someone insists a matter is simple, unless you include the study of a salad plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Eruca vesicaria is the Latin name of rocket (arugula), the salad leaf, so its biology would be literal rocket science.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday saying for something easy is turned by taking the plant called rocket at its word.

clue.text: Youth Centre in Luton extended new rises in antagonism

parts.note: the middle letter of Luton is T, extended by spelling it out in full as tee

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means moving up, so the N climbs earlier within the word

parts.note: anger is hostility or antagonism

explanation.surface: A young person at a Luton youth centre stretches out as hostility grows.
explanation.walkthrough: The T at the centre of Luton is written out as TEE; ANGER has its N ('new') moved up a place by 'rises in' to give NAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster aged thirteen to nineteen is a young person.

clue.text: Like some leaves — green, say

parts.note: eco- is the prefix for environmentally friendly, or green
to state is to say

explanation.surface: Some foliage described as verdant, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green, say' looks like an example of a leaf colour, but it gives two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany, an ecostate leaf lacks ribs, a description that applies to certain foliage.

clue.text: See 22
Long-term consumer projection

parts.note: reads like a market forecast of shopping, but means the bulge sticking out of someone who has drunk ale for years

explanation.surface: An economist's forecast of household spending over many years.
explanation.definitionFit: Years of drinking ale produce a paunch sticking out in front.

clue.text: "Sugar", they write to Spooner

indicators.note: as Dr Spooner would say it, the opening sounds of the two syllables are swapped

parts.note: biros are ballpoint pens, things that write, said as two syllables
biros are ballpoint pens, things that write, said as two syllables

explanation.surface: People address a letter to an Oxford don, calling him sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: BIROS said as 'bye-rose' has its opening sounds swapped by Spooner to make 'rye-bose', which is spelt as the sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribose is a simple five-carbon sugar found in RNA.

clue.text: The unique individual that's made single factory operative megabucks

definitions.text: The unique individual that's made single factory operative megabucks

parts.words: The unique individual that's made single factory operative megabucks
parts.note: describes an exceptional person, the rare mill worker who has struck it rich with an enormous fortune

explanation.surface: A rare person who has made an ordinary mill worker extremely wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for someone exceptional is read literally: a single mill hand earning a vast sum is a rare case among countless others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exceptional is rarer than all but a tiny fraction of people.

clue.text: See 24
The received view bears it out more than once, but it's refuted by 7

definitions.text: The received view bears it out more than once, but it's refuted by 7

parts.words: The received view bears it out more than once, but it's refuted by 7
parts.note: describes the spelling rule: the words received and view obey it, while science breaks it

explanation.surface: Conventional wisdom is repeatedly confirmed, yet a scientific discipline proves it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received' and 'view' both follow the rhyme's rule, and 7-down, SCIENCE, puts IE straight after C, breaking it.
explanation.definitionFit: The schoolroom mnemonic for English spelling is the accepted wisdom that a word such as science contradicts.

clue.text: Stray lately stealing about?

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the jumbled word swallows the abbreviation
stray means wander off, so the letters of lately go astray into a new order

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A homeless animal has recently been prowling around, thieving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' rearranges the word lately into ALLEYT, and 'stealing' has that take in the abbreviation for circa. The whole clue pictures the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban stray cat lives rough in back streets, often thieving scraps.

clue.text: See 24
Can this man judge? I'm afraid not, not quite

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: oh no is an exclamation of regretful refusal

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is able to sit in judgement and is told, apologetically, no.
explanation.walkthrough: In American slang the can is the lavatory, as is the john, which is also a man's name, hence 'this man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name doubles as US slang for a toilet, and a can is slang for that too.

clue.text: An omen, temporary accommodation allowing water through walls

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective describing something that is one

indicators.note: walls means encloses, so the water-letting word surrounds the shelter

parts.note: porous means letting liquid seep through
a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: A tent that lets in rain through its sides is a bad sign for the camping trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walls' has the seeping word enclose the camping shelter. Strictly the definition is a noun and the answer an adjective, a looseness of the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: Portentous means ominous, of the nature of a warning sign of what is to come.
